stories.title: setAuth storm causes refresh_token_already_used → self-inflicted logout
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: b1ee3217-a382-4f92-b7e1-fa73d6252840 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

After extended use with multiple projects open, the app occasionally logs itself out permanently: "Refresh token permanently dead — clearing stored tokens (refresh_token_already_used)" in the Logs panel. The user must sign in again manually.

> **Scope narrowed 2026-06-10:** three earlier fixes already mitigate the original storm — do NOT regress them:
> - `authMutex` in `src/renderer/src/lib/supabase.ts:16,51,73` — `safeSetSession()`/`safeRefresh()` serialize all session writes.
> - `setAuth` dedup at `supabase.ts:125–145` — redundant `setAuth` WS pushes with an unchanged token are skipped (`logStore.ts:68` excludes "setAuth deduped" from the anomaly counter).
> - `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` at `src/main/index.ts:26` — prevents a second Electron instance racing the same refresh token.
>
> Two concrete gaps remain (below).

## Repro (probabilistic)

With ≥5 projects (channels) open, run 50+ minutes; trigger a sync-cycle error (briefly disable Wi-Fi) that exercises `attemptSessionRefresh` while supabase-js `autoRefreshToken` fires concurrently. Log signature:
1. `setAuth #N (push)`
2. `Session restore attempt 1/1 failed: refresh_token_already_used`
3. `Stopping recovery timer — token permanently dead, sign-in required`

## Root cause — remaining gaps (verified)

**Gap 1 — `attemptSessionRefresh` bypasses the authMutex.** `src/renderer/src/services/PersonalSyncService.ts:83`:
```ts
const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.refreshSession()
```
Direct call, not `safeRefresh()`. If `autoRefreshToken` rotates at the same moment (common after wake-from-sleep), both hold the same refresh_token → one gets `refresh_token_already_used`. The `refreshAttemptedThisCycle` gate (lines 79–80) limits to one attempt per 2-minute cycle but doesn't serialize against the auto-refresher.

**Gap 2 — recovery timer never surfaces `isTokenPermanentlyDead` to React.** `src/renderer/src/services/sessionRecovery.ts:159–162`:
```ts
} else if (permanentlyDead) {
  logEvent('warn', 'sync', 'Stopping recovery timer — token permanently dead, sign-in required')
  stopRecoveryTimer()
}
```
The module flag is set, but `authStore.isTokenPermanentlyDead` is only written at `initAuth` time (authStore.ts:455). If the token dies during a live session, the SessionBanner stays amber "Sync paused" with a uselessly looping Retry instead of flipping to the red "Session expired — Sign in again" variant (SessionBanner.tsx:63–88).

## Fix plan

1. **`PersonalSyncService.ts:83`** — replace the direct call with `safeRefresh()`:
   ```ts
   import { safeRefresh } from '../lib/supabase'
   const session = await safeRefresh()
   if (!session) { /* existing failure path */ }
   await window.api.auth.storeSession(JSON.stringify({
     access_token: session.access_token, refresh_token: session.refresh_token
   }))
   authFailureCount = 0
   return true
   ```
2. **`sessionRecovery.ts`** — add `onPermanentlyDead?: () => void` to `RecoveryHandlers`; call it in the timer body when `permanentlyDead`. In **both** `startRecoveryTimer` call sites in `authStore.ts`, pass `onPermanentlyDead: () => set({ isTokenPermanentlyDead: true })`.

## Edge cases

- Keep the `refreshAttemptedThisCycle` gate.
- The power-aware reconnect (8bdf339) pauses timers during suspend; the mutex handles resume races — no extra changes.
- Don't add awaits inside the `onAuthStateChange` callback (`supabase.ts:149–170` uses `setTimeout(0)` to avoid the auth-js #762 deadlock).

## Tests

- With 6 channels subscribed, force an auth failure → exactly one `refreshSession` in logs.
- Simulate `permanentlyDead = true` in sessionRecovery → SessionBanner flips red without restart.

## Status check (2026-06-10)

PARTIALLY fixed @ HEAD d4c9f69 — storm largely mitigated by authMutex/dedup/single-instance; Gap 1 (mutex bypass at PersonalSyncService.ts:83) and Gap 2 (dead-token flag not surfaced from the recovery timer) remain.

Before marking passes: true: read ui-reference.md and debug-learnings.md. Write tests for any new repository methods or utility functions. Run npm run test — all existing and new tests must pass. Run npm run typecheck — zero errors.

All items under the description's Acceptance criteria and Tests sections are satisfied

npm run test — all existing and new tests pass

stories.title: started todoozy offline, then went online, clicked retry, connection stayed 'offline'
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 1827d14e-aa3c-4c7c-9f2e-b3d4f9eccd55 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

> "started todoozy offline, then went online, clicked retry, connection stayed 'offline'"

After starting ToDoozy offline, the "Sync paused" SessionBanner appears. After reconnecting and clicking "Retry now", the banner stays and the connection indicator stays offline — even though the session restore actually succeeded. (The 30s auto-recovery timer eventually clears the flag, but the manual button does nothing visible, and Realtime channels are never re-established by either path.)

## Repro

1. Disconnect from the internet; launch ToDoozy → offline fallback (user loaded from local SQLite), "Sync paused" banner with "Retry now".
2. Reconnect to the internet.
3. Click "Retry now" → button shows "Retrying…" then reverts; banner stays; status stays offline.

## Expected

If `tryRestoreSession(1)` succeeds: clear `isOffline`, set sync status to `synced`, drain the sync queue, and re-subscribe the Realtime channels that were skipped during offline start. If it fails: keep the banner (auto-timer continues).

## Root cause (verified, two bugs)

**Bug 1 — `handleRetry` ignores the result.** `src/renderer/src/shared/components/SessionBanner.tsx:90–98`:
```ts
const handleRetry = async (): Promise<void> => {
  if (retrying) return
  setRetrying(true)
  try {
    await tryRestoreSession(1)   // returns true on success — NEVER CHECKED
  } finally { setRetrying(false) }
}
```
On success nothing updates: `authStore.isOffline` stays true, `syncStore.status` stays offline, no queue drain.

**Bug 2 — `onRecovered` never re-subscribes Realtime.** During offline start, `subscribeToPersonalProject` bailed early (`PersonalSyncService.ts:2935`: `requireSession()` null → skip). The comment there claims the recovery timer's `onRecovered` re-runs subscriptions — it does NOT: both `onRecovered` closures in `authStore.ts` (lines 459–493 and the catch-path at ~521) only do `getUser()` + `ensureLocalUser` + `setStatus('synced')` + `isOffline: false` + `processSyncQueue()`. The App.tsx `userId` effect doesn't re-run because `userId` didn't change. Result: after recovery, sync resumes via polling only — no Realtime.

(The 2026-05-08 auth-hang fix — authTimeout/cancelLoading — is orthogonal: it prevents the splash freeze, not this.)

## Fix plan

1. **`SessionBanner.tsx:90–98`** — act on success:
   ```ts
   const restored = await tryRestoreSession(1)
   if (restored) {
     const sb = await getSupabase()
     const { data: { user } } = await sb.auth.getUser()
     if (user) {
       useSyncStore.getState().setStatus('synced')
       useAuthStore.setState({ isOffline: false })
       const { processSyncQueue } = await import('../../services/SyncService')
       processSyncQueue().catch(() => {})
       const { subscribeToPersonalProject } = await import('../../services/PersonalSyncService')
       const projects = await window.api.projects.getProjectsForUser(user.id)
       for (const p of projects.filter((p) => p.is_shared !== 1)) {
         subscribeToPersonalProject(p.id, () => {}).catch(() => {})
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. **`authStore.ts` — BOTH `onRecovered` closures (lines ~459 and ~521)** — after `set({ isOffline: false, ... })`, add the same personal-channel re-subscribe loop (try/catch, warn on failure). `subscribeToPersonalProject` has an idempotency guard (`personalChannelStates.has(projectId)`) so re-calling is a safe no-op when already subscribed.
3. **Fix the misleading comment** at `PersonalSyncService.ts:2933–2934`.
4. Shared projects: the App.tsx startup effect handles `subscribeToProject` — lower priority here, but verify shared channels also come up after recovery.

## Edge cases

- Retry while still offline → `tryRestoreSession` false → no state change; auto-timer continues.
- `isPermanentlyDead()` → returns false immediately; the red dead-token banner takes over.
- Don't double-subscribe: rely on the existing channel-state guards.

## Tests

- Mock `tryRestoreSession` → true: assert `setStatus('synced')`, `isOffline: false`, `processSyncQueue` called.
- Mock → false: assert banner state unchanged.

## Status check (2026-06-10)

PARTIALLY fixed @ HEAD d4c9f69 — auto-recovery timer covers flag/queue after ~30s, but the manual Retry button is a no-op on success (Bug 1) and Realtime channels are never re-subscribed after cold-start-offline recovery (Bug 2).

stories.title: Expand Realtime coverage: per-user channel + activity_log on personal projects
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 4c89a910-b3a8-48ea-b1f4-0847ad4e6028 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## What

Expand Supabase Realtime coverage in three areas:
1. **Per-user channel** — subscribe to user-scoped tables so cross-device changes to labels, saved views, project areas, and new-project creation appear live.
2. **activity_log on personal projects** — so MCP/Telegram/iOS-originated activity entries appear in the Detail panel without restart.
3. **task_labels on personal projects** — so label assignments made remotely (MCP) appear on task rows without waiting for the next reconcile/restart. *(Added 2026-06-10 after live observation — see Addendum.)*

## Current subscription inventory (re-verified 2026-06-10; line numbers corrected)

- **Shared projects** — `SyncService.ts:51–131` — channel `project:${projectId}`: `tasks`, `statuses`, `project_members`, `activity_log`, `project_labels`, all filtered by `project_id`. ✓
- **Personal projects** — `PersonalSyncService.ts:2785–2823` (`createPersonalChannel`) — channel `personal:${projectId}`: **`tasks` only**, filtered by project. Missing: `activity_log` (no sub, no `syncTables.ts` descriptor either), `task_labels` (no sub anywhere), `statuses` (polled/reconciled only).
- **Invites** — `SyncService.ts:630–683` — channel `invites:${email}`, `project_invites` INSERT filtered by `target_email`. ✓
- **Polling-only** (descriptors in `syncTables.ts`): `user_labels`, `user_saved_views`, `user_project_areas`, `user_settings`.
- **Covered by nothing live**: `activity_log` and `task_labels` on personal projects — remote writes reach local SQLite only via reconcile (effectively app startup).

## Consequences

- Project created from MCP/Telegram/iOS → not visible on the running desktop until restart/next poll.
- Label created from MCP → absent from pickers until next reconcile.
- Label ASSIGNED to a task from MCP → task appears live (tasks sub) but **without its label chips** until next reconcile/restart.
- Remote activity entries on personal projects → permanently missing from `DetailActivityLog`.

## Addendum — live observation (2026-06-10)

Creating a task via the remote MCP and assigning 3 labels: the task row appeared in the running app within seconds (Realtime `tasks` INSERT), but its `task_labels` rows never arrived — local table had zero rows for the task while Supabase had all three. Manual local insert rendered the chips instantly. Root constraint: **`task_labels` has no `project_id` column**, so a per-project filtered subscription isn't directly possible (and unfiltered subs are forbidden by the performance rules). Options, pick one in implementation:
- (a) **Piggyback targeted pull**: on every Realtime `tasks` INSERT/UPDATE event, also fetch that task's `task_labels` from Supabase (`.eq('task_id', id)`) and upsert locally — O(1) per event, no new subscription needed. Simplest; covers the observed case.
- (b) Add a `project_id` column to `task_labels` (Supabase migration + backfill + sync mapping) and subscribe filtered like the other tables. More invasive, fully general.
Recommendation: (a) now; consider (b) only if other task_labels staleness cases emerge.

## Implementation guide

### Part 1 — per-user channel `user:${userId}`
New `src/renderer/src/services/UserChannelService.ts` (or extend PersonalSyncService):
```ts
supabase.channel(`user:${userId}`)
  .on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'project_members', filter: `user_id=eq.${userId}` }, handleMembershipChange)
  .on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'user_labels', filter: `user_id=eq.${userId}` }, handleLabelChange)
  .on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'user_saved_views', filter: `user_id=eq.${userId}` }, handleSavedViewChange)
  .on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'user_project_areas', filter: `user_id=eq.${userId}` }, handleAreaChange)
  .subscribe(...)
```
- Membership INSERT: pull the project down (shared → `syncProjectDown` + `subscribeToProject`; personal → pull + `subscribeToPersonalProject`; distinguish by remote member count). DELETE: remove locally + tear down channel.
- Label/view/area handlers: applyRemote via IPC, rehydrate stores.
- Bootstrap in App.tsx `userId` effect after `setupRealtime()`. Guard against duplicates with a Set. Reuse the reconnect/backoff pattern from `schedulePersonalReconnect` (`PersonalSyncService.ts:2825–2876`, incl. the suspend/online gates and the `channel.state === 'joined'` auto-rejoin guard).
- Personal project creation also fires `project_members` (via `share_project` RPC inserting the owner row) — so new-project detection works for both kinds.

### Part 2 — activity_log on personal channels
Extend `createPersonalChannel` (`PersonalSyncService.ts:2785`):
```ts
.on('postgres_changes', { event: 'INSERT', schema: 'public', table: 'activity_log', filter: `project_id=eq.${projectId}` },
  async (payload) => {
    const row = payload.new as ActivityLogRow
    await window.api.activityLog.applyRemote(row).catch(() => {})  // INSERT OR IGNORE on id
    state.onChange('activity', row)
  })
```
- New IPC `activityLog:applyRemote` (`src/main/ipc-handlers.ts`) doing `INSERT OR IGNORE` by primary key (idempotent vs desktop-originated writes). Note: local `activity_log` has no `project_id` column — map only the shared fields.
- `App.tsx` onChange (~line 286): trigger `hydrateActivityLog(taskId)` when the row's `task_id` matches the open detail-panel task.

### Part 3 — task_labels targeted pull (option (a) from the Addendum)
In the personal channel's `tasks` event handler (and the shared channel's, if the same staleness applies there): after applying the task row, fetch + upsert its labels:
```ts
const { data: tls } = await supabase.from('task_labels').select('*').eq('task_id', taskRow.id)
await window.api.labels.applyRemoteTaskLabels(taskRow.id, tls ?? [])  // replace-set semantics, tombstone-aware
state.onChange('task_labels', taskRow.id)
```
Then rehydrate `hydrateAllTaskLabels(projectId)` for the affected project (debounced — reuse the existing `flushRealtime` batching).

### Part 4 — polling safety net
Add an `activity_log` descriptor to `syncTables.ts` with cursor `(project_id, created_at)` (the table has no `updated_at`).

## Constraints (Supabase performance rules)

- Every subscription filtered — never table-wide (this is why task_labels gets a targeted pull, not a sub).
- No duplicate channels (Set guard); stable channel names (no timestamps).
- Verify compound indexes exist: `user_labels(user_id, updated_at)`, `activity_log(project_id, created_at)`, `task_labels(task_id)`.
- Once the user channel is SUBSCRIBED, reduce polling frequency for the covered tables (or keep as low-frequency safety net).
- Handlers must be O(1) Supabase calls per event — no N+1.

## Edge cases

- `onRecovered` in `authStore.ts` (lines ~459, ~521) must also (re)subscribe the user channel after offline-start recovery (same gap as task 1827d14e).
- Membership DELETE for the active project: switch view away before removing.
- activity_log de-dup: rely on `INSERT OR IGNORE` by id.
- task_labels replace-set must respect local tombstones (don't resurrect a locally-deleted assignment that hasn't pushed yet).

## Files to change

`UserChannelService.ts` (new) · `PersonalSyncService.ts:2785` · `syncTables.ts` · `ipc-handlers.ts` · `preload/index.ts(+d.ts)` · `App.tsx` · `DetailActivityLog.tsx`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Project created via MCP appears in the running sidebar within ~2s
- [ ] Label created via MCP appears in pickers live
- [ ] Label assigned to a task via MCP shows as a chip on the task row within ~2s (no restart)
- [ ] MCP task activity in a personal project appears in the Detail panel within ~2s
- [ ] Membership removal removes the project live
- [ ] No duplicate activity rows; no unfiltered subscriptions

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-not-implemented @ HEAD d4c9f69. Stale line refs corrected earlier (createPersonalChannel 2448→2785; shared 48→51–131; invites 575→630; reconnect guard 2510→2864). task_labels gap confirmed live on 2026-06-10 (MCP-created task arrived without its 3 label chips; manual local insert rendered them instantly).

stories.title: Batch task-detail edits — sync only when switching tasks / closing panel / blurring app
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: d174ec02-9041-4e5c-a065-c83e41c5565c — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## What

While a task is being edited in the detail panel, batch Supabase pushes and flush only at clear boundaries (switch task / close panel / blur app / quit / 30s safety timer). Currently every status click, priority change, due-date pick, label toggle, and each 1-second keystroke burst in title/description triggers its own network push.

## Why

- Logs show "Pushed task …" after every single click in the detail panel — tens of round-trips per editing session.
- Each push is a Supabase upsert RTT; on slow networks this causes subtle UI stalls.
- Matches how Notion/Linear/Things behave: local writes instant, network sync batched.

## Current behavior (verified, file:line — corrected 2026-06-10)

- `src/renderer/src/shared/stores/taskStore.ts:274–394` — `updateTask` calls `syncIfShared(task, 'UPDATE')` at line 386 immediately after the SQLite write. No buffering. `syncIfShared` (lines 35–78) routes to `pushTask` (personal) or `syncTaskChange` (shared).
- Title: 1s debounce in `DetailTitle.tsx:37–42` → `updateTask` → push per burst (+ push on blur).
- Description: 1s debounce in `TiptapEditor.tsx:150–153` → same.
- Status/priority/due date/recurrence/reference URL: direct `updateTask` calls at `DetailPanel.tsx:230,239,243,254,258,262,266` — one push per interaction.
- Labels: `addLabel`/`removeLabel` paths push immediately via `pushTask`.
- Panel state lives in `taskStore.ts` (`showDetailPanel`, `lastSelectedTaskId`). **Note: `detailPanelStore.ts` referenced in the earlier version of this task does NOT exist.**
- `app.on('before-quit')` (`src/main/index.ts:338`) only sets `isQuitting` — no flush IPC. No `window.blur` flush listener exists.

## Implementation guide

1. **New `src/renderer/src/services/TaskBatchSyncManager.ts`:**
   - `pendingTaskIds: Set<string>`; per-task 30s safety timers (`Map<string, timeout>`)
   - `markPending(taskId)` — buffer instead of pushing while the task is open in the panel
   - `flush(taskId)` — read task, call `syncIfShared(task, 'UPDATE')`, clear pending + timer
   - `flushAll()`; `isPending(taskId)` for tests
2. **`taskStore.ts` `updateTask` (line 386):**
   ```ts
   const openTaskId = get().showDetailPanel ? get().lastSelectedTaskId : null
   if (task.id === openTaskId && !isImmediateOp(input)) {
     TaskBatchSyncManager.markPending(task.id)
   } else {
     await syncIfShared(task, 'UPDATE')
   }
   ```
   `isImmediateOp(input)` → true for `is_archived`, completion (`status_id` where `is_done === 1`), `is_in_my_day` (tray/cross-device). Create/delete always bypass (different code paths).
3. **Flush hooks:**
   - Task switch: in `selectTask`/`navigateTask`, flush the previous `lastSelectedTaskId` when the panel is open.
   - Panel close: DetailPanel Escape handler (lines 57–71) + close button → `flushAll()`.
   - App blur: `window.addEventListener('blur', () => TaskBatchSyncManager.flushAll())` in App.tsx (with cleanup).
   - Before-quit: main sends a `before-quit-flush` IPC; renderer flushes before window close.
   - Safety: `markPending` (re)sets a 30s timeout per task → `flush(taskId)`.
4. **Route label add/remove through `markPending`** when the task is open (they currently call `pushTask` directly).
5. No changes to `PersonalSyncService`/`SyncService` push APIs.

## Edge cases

- Task deleted while pending: `flush` finds no task → skip (delete already pushed its own tombstone).
- Realtime update for the same task mid-edit: store updated by `applyRemote`; next flush pushes merged state (LWW).
- Crash mid-edit: local SQLite write already happened; next startup's reconcile pushes the newer local state.
- Shared vs personal routing: `flush` calls `syncIfShared` to keep the same routing.

## Tests

`src/renderer/src/services/TaskBatchSyncManager.test.ts`:
- `markPending` idempotent; `flush` calls `syncIfShared`, clears pending+timer; `flushAll` drains; double-flush is a no-op.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Editing status→priority→label→due date→description in an open task produces ZERO "Pushed task" logs during the session
- [ ] Switching task / closing panel / blurring app → exactly ONE push for the edited task
- [ ] Quit mid-edit → flush (or sync_queue pickup next launch)
- [ ] Completion/archive/My-Day changes still push immediately

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-not-implemented @ HEAD d4c9f69 — no `TaskBatchSyncManager.ts`; `taskStore.ts:386` pushes on every update; no blur/close/quit flush hooks.

Before marking passes: true: read ui-reference.md and debug-learnings.md. Write tests for any new repository methods or utility functions. Run npm run test — all existing and new tests must pass. Run npm run typecheck — zero errors.

stories.title: MCP create_label writes legacy projects.label_data instead of project_labels junction — label invisible in app
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 2d4282aa-89dc-425f-911c-1ce498c9f78d — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## Symptom

A label created via the remote MCP edge function (`create_label`) and assigned to tasks (`assign_label_to_task`) never appears in the desktop app — not on task-row chips, not in the FilterBar, not in LabelPicker, not in Settings → Labels. Restarting the app doesn't help. The label and all its `task_labels` rows DO sync down to local SQLite correctly.

## Repro (observed live, 2026-06-10, with the "FableVerified" label)

1. Via MCP: `create_label` (project_id = Personal) → label row created in Supabase `user_labels`. ✓
2. Via MCP: `assign_label_to_task` ×46 → `task_labels` rows created. ✓
3. Desktop app syncs: local `labels` row present (correct user_id), 46 live local `task_labels` rows present. ✓
4. **Local** `project_labels` **has ZERO rows for the label** → label invisible everywhere in the UI.
5. Restart changes nothing (reconcile pulls `project_labels` from the junction table, which has no row to pull).

## Root cause (verified)

`supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts` — `LabelRepo.addToProject` (lines \~511–524) still writes the **legacy** `projects.label_data` **JSON column**:

```ts
async addToProject(projectId: string, labelId: string) {
  const label = await this.findById(labelId)
  if (!label) return
  const { data: project } = await this.client.from('projects').select('label_data').eq('id', projectId).single()
  let labelData = [...]
  if (!labelData.some((l) => l.name === label.name)) {
    labelData.push({ name: label.name, color: label.color })
    await this.client.from('projects').update({ label_data: JSON.stringify(labelData) }).eq('id', projectId)
  }
}
```

It never inserts into the `project_labels` junction table. Since v1.7.0 (commit 72097f6) the app reads project↔label links EXCLUSIVELY from `project_labels`:

- Reconcile pulls from the junction (`PersonalSyncService.ts:1485–1531`), not from `label_data`.
- Renderer queries `INNER JOIN project_labels` everywhere: `findTaskLabelsByProject` (`LabelRepository.ts:415–429`), `findAllWithUsage`, `findByProjectId` — no junction row ⇒ label filtered out of chips, pickers, and Settings.

`LabelRepo.findByProjectId` in the edge function (lines \~476–487) also still reads `label_data` — same legacy dependence on the read side (`list_labels` MCP tool may return stale/incomplete project label sets).

## Fix plan

1. `supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts` **—** `LabelRepo.addToProject`**:** replace the `label_data` JSON write with an upsert into the junction (revive tombstones):

   ```ts
   async addToProject(projectId: string, labelId: string) {
     const { error } = await this.client.from('project_labels').upsert(
       { project_id: projectId, label_id: labelId, deleted_at: null },
       { onConflict: 'project_id,label_id' }
     )
     if (error) throw new Error(`Failed to link label to project: ${error.message}`)
   }
   ```

   (Check the remote `project_labels` columns first — created_at default etc.)
2. `LabelRepo.findByProjectId`**:** read from `project_labels` joined to `user_labels` instead of parsing `projects.label_data`.
3. Decide whether to keep mirroring `label_data` for backwards compatibility with very old app builds, or drop the legacy write entirely (the current app ignores it).
4. Deploy: `supabase functions deploy mcp`.
5. **Data repair for existing rows:** any MCP-created label link that only exists in `label_data` needs a one-time backfill into `project_labels`. (The FableVerified instance was repaired manually on 2026-06-10 by inserting the local junction row; the next reconcile pushes it to Supabase.)

## Edge cases

- `create_label` reuse path (`findByName` hit) calls the same `addToProject` — fixed by the same change.
- Tombstoned link re-add: upsert with `deleted_at: null` revives it (matches the app's `TaskRepository.addLabel` upsert semantics).
- Shared projects: junction row is per-project, not per-user — same write works.

## Tests

- Edge function test: `create_label` with project_id → assert a `project_labels` row exists (not just `label_data`).
- End-to-end: MCP-created label appears in the app's FilterBar after one sync, without manual repair.

## Related tasks

- `41183299` — `addLabel` silent-drop hardening in the same file.

stories.title: Allow removing password login for OAuth users (Edge Function with service_role)
stories.description:
ToDoozy task ID: 6a8adf77-7733-4c61-be46-4ee3ae1c5628 — a corresponding ToDoozy task exists; follow the CLAUDE.md ToDoozy task lifecycle for this story (In Progress when starting, Testing while running tests, Verifying when tests pass).

## What

Let a Google-OAuth user who previously set a password REMOVE password login again (revert to Google-only sign-in). Story #65 shipped Add/Change Password; removal is the missing third leg.

## Why this needs an Edge Function

Supabase has no client-side API to clear `encrypted_password` (`auth.updateUser({ password: null })` is rejected). Only the admin API can do it, which needs the `service_role` key — never allowed in the Electron renderer.

## Current behavior (verified @ HEAD d4c9f69)

- `ProfileSettingsContent.tsx:230–275` — Password subtab has only "Change Password" / "Set Password". No removal path.
- `supabase/functions/` contains only `mcp/` and `send-password-reset/` — **no `remove-password` function exists**.
- `hasEmailIdentity` detection (line 99): `identities.some(p === 'email') || user_metadata.has_password` (aeeb404) — reliable.
- Keychain cleanup already exists: `window.api.auth.clearCredentials()` (`ipc-handlers.ts:119–138`) reads the saved email internally and deletes both the email file and Keychain entry — **no new IPC needed** (the old description's `window.api.keychain.deletePassword(email)` idea is obsolete).
- Stories #65/#66 are now verified (`passes: true`) — the old description's "awaiting verification" note is outdated.

## Implementation guide

### 1. New `supabase/functions/remove-password/index.ts` (~60 lines, model on `send-password-reset/index.ts` — same admin client + CORS setup)
- Validate caller: `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` → `adminClient.auth.getUser(jwt)`; 401 on failure.
- Guard: user must have ≥1 NON-email identity (`user.identities.some(i => i.provider !== 'email')`) — never remove the only sign-in method; return `{ ok: false, error: 'no_oauth_identity' }` otherwise.
- `adminClient.auth.admin.updateUserById(userId, { password: null })` and clear the flag: `updateUserById(userId, { user_metadata: { has_password: false } })`.
- Return `{ ok: true }`.

### 2. `ProfileSettingsContent.tsx` — Password subtab (~lines 260–274)
- Show a "Remove Password Login" (danger) button only when `hasEmailIdentity === true` AND the user has an OAuth provider (`user.identities?.some(i => i.provider !== 'email')`).
- On click: persistent confirm toast — "Remove password login? You'll only be able to sign in with Google after this." Remove (danger) / Cancel.
- On confirm: `supabase.functions.invoke('remove-password', { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${session.access_token}` } })`.
- On success: `setHasEmailIdentity(false)`; call `window.api.auth.clearCredentials()` (wipes Keychain + saved email); success toast. On failure: surface in `passwordError`.

### 3. Deploy
`supabase functions deploy remove-password`.

## Edge cases

- Email-only user: button hidden AND function rejects server-side.
- Add → remove → add password again: `has_password` metadata round-trips.
- Offline: `functions.invoke` fails → error toast.

## Tests

- Edge function: no-OAuth-identity user → rejected; Google-identity user → `updateUserById` called with `{ password: null }`; missing/invalid JWT → 401.
- UI: button visible only for `hasEmailIdentity && hasOAuthIdentity`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Google user with a password sees both "Change Password" and "Remove Password Login"
- [ ] Email-only users never see the remove option
- [ ] After removal: section reverts to "Add Password Login"; email/password sign-in fails; Google sign-in works
- [ ] Keychain entry cleared
- [ ] Edge function rejects unauthorized and email-only callers

## Status check (2026-06-10)

verified-not-implemented @ HEAD d4c9f69 — no edge function, no UI button. Description corrected: use existing `auth.clearCredentials` IPC; stories #65/#66 are verified.

stories.title: Batch review doc — before/after screenshots + repro scenarios for stories #68-#94
stories.description:
No ToDoozy task exists for this story — SKIP the ToDoozy status lifecycle entirely.

## Goal

Build the batch review/acceptance document: a single self-contained HTML report at `review/batch-review-2026-06.html` (images in `review/img/`) covering ALL 27 stories shipped on 2026-06-10/11: batch 1 = stories #68-#88 (branch ralph/audit-fixes), batch 2 = stories #89-#94 (branch ralph/sync-hardening). The user walks this doc top-to-bottom to verify each fix and move its ToDoozy task from Verifying to Done.

## Sources

- Batch-1 story list: `git show 1b008c4^:prd.json` (the prd BEFORE the fable swap — the archive folder does NOT contain it; archive/2026-06-10-audit-fixes/progress.txt DOES contain batch-1 progress notes).
- Batch-2 story list: current `prd.json` (stories 89-94).
- Per-story commit: `git log --oneline --grep="(#NN)"` — include the hash in the entry.
- Story descriptions contain ToDoozy task IDs in their header line — print each as short id in the entry so the user can find the task.

## Per-entry content (all 27)

id + title, commit hash, ToDoozy task short-id, category (fix/feature/improvement), what changed in plain language (2-4 sentences, no jargon), and ONE of three verification paths:

1. **Visually-obvious UI changes** (#71 confirmation-link color, #73 project colors, #79 tray dots, #83 context-menu rehaul, #86 archive rows, similar): TRUE before/after screenshots.
2. **Interaction bugs** (#69 scroll-wheel, #70 last-digit delete, #72 'less' click, #75/#76 NLP date chip, similar): "after" screenshot + a numbered repro scenario: do X -> before the fix Y happened -> now Z must happen.
3. **Sync/MCP/auth stories** (#74, #77, #85, #87, #88, and ALL of #89-#94): NO screenshots. Write a concrete verification scenario instead: exact MCP tool calls, two-window/two-account steps, what to check in the activity feed, Logs panel, or Supabase. Stories #88, #93, #94 are code-only with edge functions the USER must deploy first — flag these entries prominently as "DEPLOY BEFORE TESTING" and include the exact commands (`supabase functions deploy mcp` for #88/#93, `supabase functions deploy remove-password` for #94).

## Screenshot rules (CRITICAL — read before capturing anything)

- NEVER `git checkout` another commit in the main working tree. For "before" screenshots create a worktree: `git worktree add /tmp/todoozy-before <story-commit>^` then `ln -s "$(pwd)/node_modules" /tmp/todoozy-before/node_modules`, run the dev app from there (port 5200 — make sure no other dev server is running), capture, kill, `git worktree remove --force /tmp/todoozy-before`. Repeat per story needing a before-shot (batch them by commit order to minimize worktree churn).
- "After" screenshots: run the app from the main tree at HEAD. Use the project /screenshot skill to capture the ToDoozy window.
- Dev DB: `TODOOZY_DEV_DB` is already exported by ralph.sh; if missing, `export TODOOZY_DEV_DB=$(./dev-db.sh create feature)`. Never touch the production DB or the MCP server process.
- If a single before-shot is impractical after ~10 minutes of trying, fall back to after-only + written repro. Note the fallback in the entry. Do not stall the whole story on one screenshot.

## Checkpointing (CRITICAL — this story may be interrupted by usage limits and re-run)

Maintain `review/checklist.json`: `{"<story-id>": {"images": true/false, "entry": true/false}}`. Update it after EVERY captured image and finished entry. On (re)start, read it and SKIP completed work — images already in `review/img/` are done, never recapture. Write the HTML incrementally or last (it's cheap to regenerate from completed materials).

## Design requirements for the HTML

Consult the design skills before writing the HTML (global CLAUDE.md mandate): read SKILL.md of `impeccable`, `emil-design-eng`, `web-design-guidelines`, `design-taste-frontend`, plus `minimalist-ui` as the flavor. Match the ToDoozy aesthetic: minimal, monochrome-first, the project CLAUDE.md typography scale. Single self-contained HTML file, relative image paths, light/dark friendly, a sticky per-story checklist sidebar or index so the user can track acceptance progress. Order entries: batch 1 in story order, then batch 2, with the three DEPLOY-BEFORE-TESTING entries visually flagged.

## Verification for THIS story (no app source is changed)

- `npm run typecheck` once (must stay green — proves nothing was accidentally touched). Skip the dev-server compile step and skip writing Vitest tests — there is no new app code.
- passes:true requires: `review/batch-review-2026-06.html` exists; all 27 entries present, each with commit hash and a verification path; every entry that promises an image has it under `review/img/`; #88/#93/#94 flagged DEPLOY BEFORE TESTING.
- Commit `review/` + `prd.json` + `progress.txt` as `docs(review): batch 1+2 acceptance review doc (#95)`.
